hypotheses.claim: Under a 500 ms unified-deadline LNS on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 (heterogeneous scales/geometry/capacity), the destruction hook should NOT use raw |removal_savings| greedily. Instead, score_i = T(r_i)^p * g_load * g_depot * g_demand * g_rdist, where r_i is the within-instance rank-normalised removal saving r_i = |s_i| / (1 + |s_i|) (scale-free, so uniform coordinates, clustered coordinates and mixed-demand instances contribute comparably), T(r) = r/(1-r) is a bounded rank-power transform, and the exponent p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio) = p_lo + (p_hi - p_lo) * clip(stagnation_ratio,0,1) interpolates from p_lo ~ 1.0 (sharp, worst-first removal while improvements are still flowing) to p_hi > 1 flattening the top of the ranking (quasi-random removal) as stagnation_ratio -> 1. Rank-power flattening under stagnation is exactly the mechanism that escapes R2R local optima without an RNG, so it should beat the zero-evolution L3-ctrl Worst-Cost Removal skeleton and the plain rank-1 variant on the mean tour length, with the largest per-instance gains on the clustered/high-capacity-heterogeneity regime; conversely p_hi too large (fully uniform) must lose on uniform-random instances because destroying non-critical customers wastes the deterministic Regret-2 repair budget, so p_hi must be capped.
